subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should identical exec arguments with the same structured nonzero outcome count as no progress even when their output changes between calls?
rationale: Source and live proof establish the bug and implementation, but code alone cannot decide whether changing output from commands such as diff-style tools is meaningful progress or volatile failure noise; this choice changes when OpenClaw may block an agent run.

options.title: Accept Structured Nonzero Hashing
options.body: Refresh and merge the branch after explicitly accepting that output changes do not constitute progress while the command keeps returning the same nonzero outcome.

options.title: Narrow The Classifier
options.body: Revise the patch to ignore output only for explicitly classified failure outcomes, accepting that ordinary exit-1 SSH, Docker, or grep loops may remain harder to detect.

options.title: Preserve Current Semantics
options.body: Keep nonzero output-sensitive hashing and close this approach, leaving the linked runaway-loop issue for a different detector policy.

recommendation.title: Accept Structured Nonzero Hashing
recommendation.body: Refresh and merge the branch after explicitly accepting that output changes do not constitute progress while the command keeps returning the same nonzero outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed the exact foreground contract and have recent ownership signals in both agent and exec runtime history.
